rules.statement: a. Every `amount` is a JSON number, never a string, with no unit or currency symbol: remove thousands separators, and write parentheses or a leading minus as a negative number (`3,624` is 3624; `(211)` is -211). Money amounts are written as the source prints them, in the `unit` and `currency` of the source scope the book binds to (rule i; a facility's in the facility's own `currency`), and are never arithmetic. Other amounts have their own unit: `effective_tax_rate` is a decimal fraction (21.0% is 0.21); a facility's `spread_bps` and `floor_bps` are basis points (2.75% is 275) and its `fixed_rate` is a percent (5.25% is 5.25); an FX `rate` is target-currency units per source-currency unit; a KPI amount is in that KPI's own `unit`.

b. `accounts[].metric_id` is one of the account metrics the schema's `metric_id` enum lists: the r14 canonical accounts Python calculates from. A figure the filing reports that has no account metric belongs in `statement_lines` under its own `item_id` (issuer detail with the `other:` prefix), with its `statement` and `sign_convention`, not in `accounts`.
c. Every `period_id` an entry uses must be declared in its book's `periods`.

d. A statement line's `sign_convention` is `signed` when its amount carries the arithmetic sign the statement implies (an expense or outflow negative, a revenue or inflow positive); balance-sheet lines are always `signed`. Use `outflow_magnitude` only when the source prints an expense or outflow as a positive magnitude and you keep that presentation: then `sign_citations` must hold at least one located span showing the printed presentation (repeat the value's citation in `sign_citations`), never empty. A negative amount under `outflow_magnitude` is read as -abs(amount); use `signed` for a negative figure. A positive `signed` amount on a line of an outflow account (IS `cogs`, IS `depreciation_amortization`, IS `opex_including_da`, IS `operating_lease_cost`, CFS `dividends_paid`, CFS `cash_taxes_paid`, CFS `cash_interest_paid`, CFS `lease_payments_in_financing`, CFS `interest_paid_in_financing`, CFS `capex_total`) is refused, never flipped: where the source prints that outflow as a positive magnitude, use `outflow_magnitude` with `sign_citations`; where it prints a net inflow on that line (a refund), record that period's value as status `missing` with a null `amount` and a `reason` saying the source prints a net inflow, never a negative or zero figure (for an `extract_statements` row, leave the row out of its unit's `rows` in `unit_maps` and write its lines yourself, citing the row). `outflow_magnitude` is also refused on a line of an outflow account whose label states an inflow: one of the words `refund`, `refunds`, `refunded`, `received`, `receipt`, `receipts`, `proceeds`, `inflow`, `inflows`, `reimbursement`, `reimbursements`, in any letter case, outside a "net of" clause (the clause runs to the bracket that encloses it, a semicolon or the end of the label, so "Cash taxes paid, net of refunds received" stays an outflow magnitude). Such a line is `signed` with the negative amount where the source prints the figure negative; otherwise it is a net inflow, recorded as status `missing` with a null `amount` and a `reason` as above.

e. A statement line is one row per period under one `line_id` and one `display_priority`: every period's row for it repeats the same `statement`, `item_id`, `label` and `line_kind`, and a period is never its own `line_id`. For example `line_id` "is-net-revenues" has a row for FY2025 and a row for FY2024, both at `display_priority` 1. An `item_id` is used by one line per statement (one `other:` id per issuer-detail line, never reused). `display_priority` is unique within a statement across all periods (two lines of one statement never share a number). Addbacks (`addback_id`), segments (`segment_id`) and KPIs (`kpi_id`) follow the same rule: one id and one `display_priority` across all periods, never repeated for another id, and every period's row repeats the same `addback_label` and `classification` (addbacks), `segment_name` and `segment_type` (segments), or `kpi_label`, `business_unit`, `definition`, `unit` and `value_type` (KPIs).

f. A statement line's `item_id` is one of the ids listed for its own `statement` below; an id listed for one statement is not admitted on another unless that statement lists it too. A line the filing prints that is not in its statement's list takes an `other:` id (for example `other:deferred_revenue`; letters, digits and `_.:-` only, no spaces), never another statement's id.
IS: revenue, cogs, gross_profit, sga, other_operating, ebitda_reported, ebitda_adjusted, depreciation_amortization, ebit, interest_expense_total, interest_expense_cash, interest_income, other_non_operating, pretax_income, income_tax_total, income_tax_cash, net_income, exceptionals, sbc, opex_including_da, operating_lease_cost
CFS: ocf_before_wc, cfo_ncfo, working_capital_change, capex_maintenance, capex_growth, capex_total, fcf_levered, fcf_unlevered, dividends_paid, acquisitions, disposals, debt_issuance, debt_repayment, equity_issuance, equity_buybacks, net_cash_change, cash_taxes_paid, cash_interest_paid, investing_cash_flow, financing_cash_flow, fx_cash_effect, opening_cash, closing_cash, net_income, lease_payments_in_financing, interest_paid_in_financing
BS: cash_and_equivalents, restricted_cash, short_term_investments, trade_receivables, inventory, other_current_assets, total_current_assets, ppe_net, goodwill, other_intangibles, other_noncurrent_assets, total_assets, short_term_debt, current_portion_long_term_debt, trade_payables, other_current_liabilities, total_current_liabilities, senior_secured_debt, senior_unsecured_debt, subordinated_debt, total_debt, pension_obligations, lease_obligations, other_noncurrent_liabilities, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity, minority_interests, total_equity, rcf_drawn, rcf_commitment, net_accounts_receivable, accounts_payable, restricted_cash_noncurrent

g. An `accounts` entry and the statement line linked to it (the same metric and `period_id`; a line is usually linked to the account named like its `item_id`; the renamed links are: IS `ebitda_reported` is the `ebitda` account, IS `ebitda_adjusted` is the `adjusted_ebitda` account, IS `income_tax_total` is the `income_tax_expense` account, CFS `capex_total` is the `capex_and_intangible_investment` account) must carry the same amount, an outflow compared as a negative number (for example the IS `income_tax_total` line and the `income_tax_expense` account). When the source gives two values, write the disagreement explicitly: set that observation's `status` to `conflicting` with a null `amount`, a `reason` and at least two distinct located `alternatives` (each with an `amount`, `citations` and an `explanation`), never two silent values. A statement line whose `status` is `conflicting` leaves the matching `accounts` amount null (`conflicting` or `missing`), never a canonical value. Likewise a line of an outflow account withheld as `missing` (rule d: a net inflow such as a refund) leaves that period's `accounts` entry of its account out or with a null `amount`, never a figure the statement withholds.

h. `segment_allocation` places every `segment_id` exactly once: each segment appears in exactly one slot's `component_segment_ids`, no segment is left out or listed twice, and each keeps its own presentation row in `segments`. A `slot_id` is used at most once.

i. Python fills each book's and each period's `currency`, `unit`, `accounting_basis` and `entity_perimeter` (they are not in the schema) with the strings of the step:source_context `scopes` entry they bind to: a `historical_duration` or `period_end` scope of the entity in the book's `binding.books[].entity_id` with the period's `end_date`, and, unless `period_type` is `PERIOD_END`, a `historical_duration` scope with the period's `start_date` too (a book takes the four strings its periods share). Choose that entity and each period's `period_type`, `start_date` and `end_date` so that they name such a scope, write money amounts in that scope's `unit` and `currency`, and keep in one book only periods whose scopes carry the same four strings: a period with no such scope, or a book whose periods' scopes differ, is a rejection.

j. The quoted words must appear on the cited page. A statement or reconciliation heading printed at the foot of the preceding page is not on the table's page: quote a row label or a figure from the table's own page, or cite the heading's own page.

k. Statement lines come from `extract_statements`: take each amount from the line's raw_values, written as rule a says, never retyped from memory or prose. For the qualified path select exact `label_candidates` parts in `row_label_selections`; Python joins the selected printed fragments and cites each fragment. Choose each row's `quantity` kind and scale from its printed unit context, not its metric name. You map `item_id`/`period_id`, choose `line_kind` and `sign_convention`, and cite the page. A value no extracted line holds keeps its rule f `item_id`, is read with `read_pages` and cited there, and carries a limitation saying it was not extracted. Verify a line the tool flags with `read_pages` before using it.

Map every statement unit `extract_statements` returns in `unit_maps`; Python then writes its statement lines from the extracted text. For each unit give its `source_id` and `locator`, the `book_id`, the `statement` (BS, IS or CFS; comprehensive income is IS), `columns` with one period_id from that book per printed column, or null when the book declares no period for it or another unit already gives that period, and `rows` with each extracted row's number and its `line_id` (used once in its book), `item_id`, `line_kind` and `sign_convention` (total liabilities and equity is `other:total_liabilities_and_equity`). For the qualified path set `profile` to `typed-source/1`. Then supply exactly one `row_label_selections` entry for every mapped row: `row` is the extracted row's physical `line_no`, and `part_line_numbers` selects the ordered contiguous exact fragments shown in that row's `label_candidates`, including its amount-bearing line. Python joins only those printed fragments with single spaces; do not supply reconstructed label text or select a section caption as a row prefix. Supply exactly one `row_dimensions` entry per mapped row, with a `quantity` kind (`monetary`, `currency_per_share`, or `shares`), source-supported scale and citations to the statement's printed unit context. A per-share label must use `currency_per_share`; a weighted-average share count must use `shares`; ordinary statement amounts use `monetary`. Balance-sheet columns bind only to `PERIOD_END` periods with no start date. Flow columns must match the printed duration and exact end date; cite source fiscal policy for annual period starts. Comprehensive income uses the transport statement `IS` only with distinct `other:ci_*` line and item IDs and its own page/unit. Do not write lines for the rows you map. Write a `statement_lines` entry only for a row Python leaves to you (the submit result's notes name each one): the row's statement, its label verbatim, each mapped column's amount (a printed dash is 0), citing the row's own locator (on a line source, `line:N` with N the row's number in the extract), citing each selected fragment and the amount-bearing line. A row left uncovered is refused as an `Uncovered extracted statement line` with its reason.
